exam.title: Python for Data Analysis — Validated 50Q Sample
exam.description: Validated production form used to define the dynamic Python Track Exam selection profile.

questions.question: A learner writes `true` and expects a Boolean. What is the correction?

options.text: Use `TRUE()`
Use `"True"` to get bool
Use `True` with a capital T.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. Boolean literals هما True وFalse بحرف أول Capital.

questions.question: A student expects `text[1:4]` to include index 4. What rule fixes the mistake?

options.text: The start index is excluded
All slices include both ends
Strings cannot be sliced
The end index in a slice is excluded.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. String indexing يبدأ من 0، والـ end في slicing غير مشمول.

questions.question: If the user types `20`, what does `age = input()` store?

options.text: The integer 20
The string `"20"`
The float 20.0
The Boolean True

explanation.ar: input() ترجع String، والتحويل الصريح مثل int() مطلوب قبل arithmetic numeric.

questions.question: What type of result should a simple condition such as `x > 0` produce?

options.text: List
Boolean
Dictionary
Tuple

explanation.ar: Control flow تختار blocks للتنفيذ بناءً على conditions.

questions.question: For `number=5`, what is `number > 0`?

options.text: False
True

explanation.ar: if تنفذ block فقط عندما condition=True.

questions.question: What is `len("Alice")`?

explanation.ar: المصدر يطبق if على len(string) وعلى التحقق من None.

source.reference: Slides 7–8 — String Length and None checks

questions.question: A learner expects `range(5)` to include 5. What rule fixes this?

options.text: The start value is excluded
range only works on strings
range always starts at 1
The stop value in range is excluded.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. for loop تتكرر على sequence مثل list/string/range وتنفذ block لكل item.

questions.question: A student expects loop-else to run after break. What is the correction?

options.text: else always runs twice
break only skips one print
for cannot have else
break prevents the natural-completion else.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. Loop else تنفذ عند natural completion بدون break.

questions.question: A while condition remains True forever because the counter is never changed. What is the main risk?

options.text: Tuple mutation
Set sorting
Automatic exit after one iteration
Infinite loop

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. while تكرر block طالما condition=True وتناسب عدد iterations غير المعروف مسبقًا.

source.reference: Slides 13–14 — while loop and basic example

questions.question: For `[3,5,2,8,1,9,4]`, what maximum is found?

explanation.ar: max_value تبدأ بأول عنصر وتتحدث فقط عند العثور على قيمة أكبر.

questions.question: What vowel count is shown for `Hello, how are you?`?

explanation.ar: الـ loop تمر على كل char وتزيد counter فقط إذا char.lower() داخل aeiou.

questions.question: Which primes are shown from 10 to 20?

explanation.ar: Prime checker يستخدم outer range loop وinner divisor loop، مع break عند وجود divisor وelse عند عدم وجوده.

source.reference: Slide 7 — Prime Numbers in a Range

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Function Definition` according to the taught session?

options.text: A function is a reusable block of code defined to perform a specific task.
Parameters let a function receive values, and `return` sends a result back to the caller.
A default parameter provides a value used when the caller omits that argument.
A function can return multiple values that the caller can unpack into separate variables.

explanation.ar: A function is a reusable block of code defined to perform a specific task.

questions.question: If `greet(name="Guest")` is called with no argument, which name is used?

options.text: None
name
Guest
An error always

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `Default Parameters` behavior: A default parameter provides a value used when the caller omits that argument.

questions.question: The taught divide example returns quotient and remainder. What receives them?

options.text: One set only
A comment
Two variables such as q and r
A file object

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `Multiple Return Values` behavior: A function can return multiple values that the caller can unpack into separate variables.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Average Function` according to the taught session?

options.text: A function can aggregate a list of numbers and return their average.
The function scans words and returns the longest one encountered.
The taught `is_prime(n)` checks divisibility up to the square root and returns a Boolean.
Two functions convert Celsius↔Fahrenheit and return converted numeric values.

explanation.ar: A function can aggregate a list of numbers and return their average.

questions.question: What Boolean output is shown for the taught prime example?

options.text: False
None
True

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `Prime Function` behavior: The taught `is_prime(n)` checks divisibility up to the square root and returns a Boolean.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to perform the taught basic email-format check?

options.text: frequency dictionary
"@" in email and "." after @
key=lambda x: ...
sum(numbers) / len(numbers)

explanation.ar: `"@" in email and "." after @` is the course-aligned choice for this task: perform the taught basic email-format check.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `open() & Modes` according to the taught session?

options.text: `open(path, mode)` opens a file; default mode is read (`r`) if omitted.
`file.close()` closes a file object and releases resources; `f.closed` reports whether it is closed.
`read()` reads file content; `read(n)` can read only a limited number of characters.
A `with` statement automatically handles closing the file and reduces resource-leak risk.

explanation.ar: `open(path, mode)` opens a file; default mode is read (`r`) if omitted.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `close()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `file.close()` closes a file object and releases resources; `f.closed` reports whether it is closed.
`read()` reads file content; `read(n)` can read only a limited number of characters.
A `with` statement automatically handles closing the file and reduces resource-leak risk.
`w` truncates existing content before writing; `a` appends at the end without removing existing content.

explanation.ar: `file.close()` closes a file object and releases resources; `f.closed` reports whether it is closed.

questions.question: What does `file.read(10)` request?

options.text: 10 lines necessarily
A 10-byte file creation
The first/next 10 characters from the current position
10 directory names

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `read()` behavior: `read()` reads file content; `read(n)` can read only a limited number of characters.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `NumPy ndarray` according to the taught session?

options.text: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.
`shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.
`np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

explanation.ar: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Array Shape` according to the taught session?

options.text: `shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.
`np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.
`np.linspace()` creates a requested number of evenly spaced values between two endpoints.

explanation.ar: `shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.

questions.question: What does `np.arange(0,10,2)` produce?

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `np.arange()` behavior: `np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Indexing & Slicing` according to the taught session?

options.text: NumPy supports 1D indexing/slicing and 2D row/column indexing for subsetting arrays.
NumPy applies arithmetic element-wise and can broadcast compatible scalars/smaller shapes across larger arrays.
`np.dot()` performs dot product/matrix multiplication and is used in linear algebra and prediction examples.
NumPy provides mean/sum/max/min and is applied to score analysis, growth, temperature, normalization and reshaping.

explanation.ar: NumPy supports 1D indexing/slicing and 2D row/column indexing for subsetting arrays.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to perform vectorized element-wise arithmetic?

options.text: np.dot(a, b)
arr + scalar / array operations
np.mean()/np.sum()/np.max()/np.min()
np.array(...)

explanation.ar: `arr + scalar / array operations` is the course-aligned choice for this task: perform vectorized element-wise arithmetic.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Series` according to the taught session?

options.text: A Pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array that can hold data values.
A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled table with columns that may have different types.
`head()` returns the first five rows by default for a quick preview.
`info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.

explanation.ar: A Pandas Series is a one-dimensional labeled array that can hold data values.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to preview the first rows of a DataFrame?

options.text: df.info()
df.head()
df.describe()
df["column"] / df[condition]

explanation.ar: `df.head()` is the course-aligned choice for this task: preview the first rows of a DataFrame.

questions.question: Which detail is explicitly provided by `info()`?

options.text: Only mean salary
Only sorted rows
Data types and non-null counts
Only file size

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `info()` behavior: `info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `loc[]` according to the taught session?

options.text: `loc[]` is label-based indexing for selecting specific rows and columns.
Pandas supports adding columns, vectorized column updates, and dropping columns with `drop(..., axis=1)`.
`isnull()` detects missing values, `fillna()` fills them, and `dropna()` removes rows with missing values.
`groupby()` groups rows for aggregation; `apply()` applies a custom function to values/structures.

explanation.ar: `loc[]` is label-based indexing for selecting specific rows and columns.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to add, update or remove DataFrame columns?

options.text: isnull()/fillna()/dropna()
df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)
groupby() / apply()
pd.Series(...)

explanation.ar: `df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: add, update or remove DataFrame columns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `CSV Loading` according to the taught session?

options.text: The applied workflow loads CSV data into a DataFrame and begins with head/info/describe inspection.
A Boolean condition on the Department column filters the DataFrame to matching employees.
Grouping by Department then taking mean Salary produces average salary for each department.
A new salary column can be calculated vectorially by multiplying Salary by 1.05.

explanation.ar: The applied workflow loads CSV data into a DataFrame and begins with head/info/describe inspection.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Department Filtering` according to the taught session?

options.text: A Boolean condition on the Department column filters the DataFrame to matching employees.
Grouping by Department then taking mean Salary produces average salary for each department.
A new salary column can be calculated vectorially by multiplying Salary by 1.05.
`sort_values()` orders rows by a chosen column, including descending age in the example.

explanation.ar: A Boolean condition on the Department column filters the DataFrame to matching employees.

questions.question: What aggregation is used after grouping in the taught example?

options.text: sum() only
head()
mean()
to_csv()

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `groupby Mean` behavior: Grouping by Department then taking mean Salary produces average salary for each department.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Datetime Conversion & Filtering` according to the taught session?

options.text: `pd.to_datetime()` converts the date column before filtering rows after a date threshold.
`to_csv()` writes a DataFrame to a CSV; `index=False` excludes the row index.
The Hospital case study applies inspection, filtering, aggregation, calculated fields, sorting/date logic and export in one workflow.
The Restaurant case study applies Pandas manipulation to sales/customer analysis as an integrated applied workflow.

explanation.ar: `pd.to_datetime()` converts the date column before filtering rows after a date threshold.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to export a DataFrame without the index column?

options.text: multi-step Pandas workflow
df.to_csv(..., index=False)
multi-step sales/customer workflow
pd.read_csv(...)

explanation.ar: `df.to_csv(..., index=False)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: export a DataFrame without the index column.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Data Visualization Foundations` according to the taught material?

options.text: Data visualization represents data graphically to uncover patterns, trends, and insights.
It is presented as a file-system permission command.
It is a Python container whose main purpose is key-value storage.
It is taught as a replacement for every data-analysis step.

explanation.ar: Data visualization represents data graphically to uncover patterns, trends, and insights. ده هو الاستخدام/التعريف المدعوم في الجزء المشار له من المصدر.

source.reference: Slides 5–6 — What is Data Visualization? / Objectives
